chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu'l-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him),
that he was asked: What is the intellect? He said: Suppressing grief, speaking gently to enemies, and showing kindness to friends.

key_terms.التجرع للغصة: Suppressing grief/swallowing bitterness - enduring hardship with patience and composure
key_terms.العقل: The intellect ('aql) - in Islamic tradition, encompasses reason, wisdom, and sound judgment in both thought and action
key_terms.مداراة: Showing kindness/good social conduct - maintaining warm and supportive relations with friends
key_terms.مداهنة: Speaking gently/diplomatic flattery - treating enemies with soft speech to avoid conflict

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the definition of intellect ('aql)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) was asked to define the intellect ('aql). Rather than giving an abstract philosophical definition, he defined it through three practical social behaviors: enduring hardship without complaint, treating adversaries with diplomatic gentleness, and being supportive and caring toward one's companions. This definition reflects the classical Shia understanding of 'aql as practical wisdom governing interpersonal conduct, not merely theoretical reasoning.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from `Ali b. Mu`abbad from al-Husayn b. Khalid from Abi’l Hasan al-Rida (as).
He was asked: What is the intellect? So, he said: Suppressing grief, speaking gently to enemies, and showing support to friends.
